instrument_reproduction: `python org/missions/D14/LGIC/LGIC_ENFORCE/deliverables/0.9.0_WK_LGIC_ENFORCE~1/r6_campaign_resolve.py record` regenerates this file's three lists BYTE-FOR-BYTE from any checkout at or after the pin, INCLUDING after its own `mint` verb has run. That is deliberate and it is the one thing about this instrument worth knowing: leg B reads resources.json to learn which IAM roles already carry a system, and `mint` WRITES resources.json -- so the read is taken at the PIN via `git show a981b05ee8:<path>` rather than from the worktree. Read from the worktree it would measure its own output, a re-run would find its own 32 rows already present and report ZERO resolutions, and a later reader checking this record would get a different answer with nothing to explain it.

The two figures are equal BY CONSTRUCTION of the population, not by luck, and a later census over NAMING_CENSUS_REPORT will report a SMALLER brace-carrying population than 1370 -- that is a different denominator over a different instrument and is not this one.

non_system_disposition.rule: NOT A TIMEBOX AND NOT ONE REMEDY. The disposition of this class is: EACH ROW IS TRANSFERRED TO THE CARRIER ITS OWN TOKEN NAMES, and that carrier is named per token in `token_carriers` from NAMING_SCHEMA.json grade.placeholder -- {system} from resources.json (IN this grant), {scope}/{source} from THE BUCKET, {cadence} from THE SCHEDULE (both OUT of this grant, which is systems.json and resources.json only). THE ACT A LATER CENSUS TAKES, per group of `partition_by_remedy`, no re-derivation needed: SCOPE_OR_SOURCE_ONLY (112) -- cut a cell granted the bucket read and substitute from the object's own address; CADENCE_ONLY (57) -- cut a cell granted the schedule read and map schedule_expression onto cadence.values; CADENCE_PLUS_SYSTEM (51) -- BOTH of those, in either order, because one alone leaves a brace; UNSANCTIONED_BRACE_NOT_A_PLACEHOLDER (15) -- do NOT look for a source, it does not exist; these are template format fields and the question is whether the census should grade them at all (surprise row LGIC_ENFORCE-W1-S70). THE MECHANICAL TEST that keeps this from being a label, runnable by any later reader: for a row, the group is decided by its canonical's brace tokens alone -- set(tokens) - {'system','source','scope','cadence'} non-empty is group 4, else 'cadence' and 'system' both present is group 3, else 'cadence' present is group 2, else group 1. No judgment, no owner's opinion, and the four counts sum to the printed denominator 235.
non_system_disposition.rule_summary: NOT A TIMEBOX. This class is BLOCKED ON A CARRIER, not on effort, and the blocking carrier is DIFFERENT PER TOKEN -- so it is dispositioned per token, by subtraction from its own printed denominator, and no amount of round-7 budget moves any of it.
non_system_disposition.authority: org/standards/NAMING_SCHEMA.json grade.placeholder, quoted: 'a canonical_form may carry {system}, {source}, {scope} or {cadence} ONLY for a slot the name does not carry. Each is a typed gap, never a guess, filled from its source: {system} from the identity registry's resource-to-system rows (LGIC_ENFORCE), {source}/{scope} from the bucket, {cadence} from the schedule.' FOUR tokens are sanctioned placeholders. That enumeration is the domain the subtraction below runs over, and it is the schema's, not this cell's.

system.declared_carrier: infra/logic/registry/resources.json -- the identity registry's resource-to-system rows, keyed (name, type) at lib/opal_naming.py:1030-1032
system.act: mint a (name, type, system, evidence) row, which is exactly what this cell's 25 resolutions did

source.declared_carrier: THE BUCKET (same clause as {scope}). systems.json supplies the vocabulary -- its own _about says a row is 'every token that may fill a resource name's {system} slot or a key's {source}'
source.act: read the key's first segment from the live address or the producer, then check it against a systems.json VENDOR/PRODUCT/PLATFORM_SUBSYSTEM row

scope.declared_carrier: THE BUCKET the key sits in -- not a registry file. scopes.json supplies the VOCABULARY the value must belong to (9 rows), never the value
scope.act: read the object's own bucket/prefix from the live S3 address or the producer's declared output path, then check the value against a scopes.json row's LONG form (NAMING_SCHEMA.json key.scope_form LONG)

cadence.declared_carrier: THE SCHEDULE -- the EventBridge rule's or the schedule's own expression, not a registry file. NAMING_SCHEMA.json cadence.values supplies the vocabulary (daily, weekly, monthly, hourly) plus the on-{event} form
cadence.act: read the rule's schedule_expression from its Terraform declaration (or `aws events describe-rule`, read-only) and map it onto cadence.values

partition_by_remedy._written_as: the printed denominator 235 MINUS each group, never a forward list of groups recalled (Rule 24(i)); the groups are disjoint by construction (one elif chain per row) and the remainder is asserted below

SCOPE_OR_SOURCE_ONLY.remedy: read {scope}/{source} off THE BUCKET per grade.placeholder. OUT OF THIS GRANT: no bucket read and no scopes.json write is in this order's <paths>.

CADENCE_ONLY.remedy: read {cadence} off THE SCHEDULE per grade.placeholder. OUT OF THIS GRANT.

CADENCE_PLUS_SYSTEM.remedy: TWO carriers, and this is the group the class name hides: the {system} half IS in this grant (a resources.json row) and the {cadence} half is NOT. So neither remedy alone clears one of these rows, and minting the system half here would have recorded 51 resolutions that still carry a brace -- which is why they are carded whole rather than half-resolved.

UNSANCTIONED_BRACE_NOT_A_PLACEHOLDER.remedy: NOT A SUBSTITUTION AT ALL and NO declared source exists for it, now or later. See surprise row LGIC_ENFORCE-W1-S70. These carry a brace token OUTSIDE grade.placeholder's four ({snap}, {dim_name}, {d}, {dc}, {firm}); measured discriminator: the brace is already present in the row's OWN `current` (the name as declared), which is true of 15 of 235 rows in this class and, read UNSCOPED over all 1370 carried rows, of those rows and no others. They are python format fields in a producer's key TEMPLATE, so the census graded a format string rather than a key. The remedy is a census-domain question for the registry owner, not a lookup.

non_system_disposition.carried_as: carded (with owner and reason), never deferred -- deferral is the timebox's word

resolution_rule.what_counts_as_MEASURED: two independent legs onto a DECLARED source, never the token's shape. LEG A: the resource is declared at a Terraform file:line named by infra/aws/lambda/ci/lambda-source-map.json's tf_file, or is an infra/aws/ec2/EC2_MANIFEST.json service entry with a source_path. LEG B: the system is already carried by that resource's OWN IAM role, which is an existing infra/logic/registry/resources.json row with its own cited evidence -- a Lambda's role is declared in the same module block as the function, so these are one resource's two faces. LEG C, recorded where found and never required: the tf_file's header names the owning project code.
resolution_rule.why_not_the_prefix: the leading token of these names is a SCOPE, not a system, and reading it as a system would be exactly the shape-inference this rule exists to exclude: cot-pipeline alone carries both etfs rows (cot-etf-ownership-daily-role) and mdpf rows (cot-rebalancer-runner-role) in this registry, so `cot-` resolves no system at all.
resolution_rule.selection_order: deterministic: sorted by (source kind, resource name), first 25 distinct resources taken. Stated because the cut between resolved and deferred is otherwise a hidden choice.

mint_target.key: (name, type) -- lib/opal_naming.py:1030-1032 indexes resources.json on that pair and :1147 reads it only where the name's own tokens resolve no system
mint_target.fence_clearance_R29: MEASURED that this mint cannot change a generated policy on an applied resource: infra/aws/terraform/modules/opal_name/generated_locals.tf:1 declares its own inputs as 'over exemptions.json,scopes.json' and resources.json is not one; the only plan-time read of the registry anywhere under infra/aws/terraform/ is modules/opal_name/main.tf:82 jsondecode(file(.../exemptions.json)); resources.json reaches Terraform only in two GENERATED TEST FIXTURES and no round-6 cell runs `generate`. exemptions.json is not written by this cell and the c33-fence arm grades that against the pinned base independently.

timebox.budget_reading: 25 MEASURED RESOLUTIONS = 25 distinct resources, the reading round 5 took (its own record: 41 resolved census rows across 25 distinct resources). Recorded because check_en_r6.py's arm implements the bar as start + 25 over the resolved LIST, which at a start of 1370 is 1395 and cannot bind a list that partitions 1370 rows -- so the arm's STOPPED branch is the one that grades, and the prose budget is what actually bounds this cell.

delta_riding_next_round.note: the remainder rides round 7. Of it, the candidates already MEASURED this round carry their full two-leg chain in their own reason_detail, so round 7 mints them without re-deriving anything.
